newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Mining said reconsidering Bakun stake.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Mining said reconsidering Bakun stake.

text.p: Malaysia Mining Corp Bhd is reconsidering its planned five percent equity stake in the Bakun hydroelectric dam holding company, the Singapore Business Times said on Monday.

The newspaper quoted sources as saying Malaysia Mining was not keen to pay the 200 million ringgit, or two ringgit per share, price for the stake in Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd, comprising 100 million shares.

Malaysia Mining had been hoping for a lower price, the Times said. If it drops out of the shareholding structure, its stake might be given to another party or to Ekran Bhd, the main contractor for the Bakun dam, the newspaper said.
The $5.5 billion-dam is to be built in the East Malaysia state of Sarawak on Borneo island.
Officials at Malaysia Mining and Ekran were not available for comment on Monday.

Ekran has the biggest slice of the project, a 32 percent stake. Various groups in Sarawak will hold 28 percent with smaller amounts held by the national pension fund and the state electric utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
Tenaga earlier this month reduced its equity holding in the dam company to five percent from 25 percent.
The dam company is offering a total of four billion shares in a two-tranche stock issue. Its initial stock listing is expected to take place next year.
